verse.text: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.

reflection.scripture: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
reflection.observation: Jesus calls us to mirror the character of God Himself — not just to act merciful when it's convenient, but to embody mercy as a way of life. This comes right after Jesus teaches about loving enemies and doing good without expecting anything in return. Mercy isn't a transaction; it's a reflection of who our Father is. The standard isn't human fairness — it's divine compassion.
reflection.application: Today, look for one person who doesn't 'deserve' your kindness — someone who has been difficult, overlooked, or wronged you. Extend mercy without keeping score. In your journaling, write down how it felt to release the expectation of reciprocity. Remember: mercy flows from having first received it.
reflection.prayer: Father, You have shown me mercy I could never earn. Help me become someone who gives it as freely as I've received it. Soften my heart where it's grown hard, and remind me that every person I meet is someone You love deeply. Let my life look more like Yours today. Amen.
